messages:
leo: Quick question — I have a dentist appointment tomorrow at 11am, looks like I'd be out for ~3 hours. Does our PTO policy allow using partial-day sick instead of a full-day? I don’t want to burn a full vacation day.

zara: @leo yes, partial-day sick is supported. We track in 15-min increments. Use the Time Off form and set it as "Sick (partial day)". Your balance will deduct the actual hours you log. :tooth:

manager-amy: Also please add a quick note in the team calendar and ping the on-call so we can swap coverage if needed. I can approve the time off once you file.

leo: Filing now. One follow-up: I started as a contractor earlier this year and converted to FT last month — do my accruals pro-rate differently for partial days given the conversion? Payroll mentioned rounding rules before.

people-ops: Good catch. Policy summary: FT employees accrue sick/PTO monthly based on hire date and FTE. When someone converts from contractor to FT mid-month, accruals begin pro-rated from conversion date; partial-day deductions still use the logged hours. Rounding rules: payroll rounds accrual balances to nearest 0.25 hour for display, but accounting keeps internal precision. In practice you should see the exact hours deducted from your visible balance (rounded display).

people-ops: To be explicit: 1) Submit partial-day request with start/end times; 2) Manager approval required for scheduling; 3) Payroll handles accrual pro-rating at conversion and will not double-charge for contractor period.

payroll-bot: Payroll note: Conversion processed 2026-01-12. Starting balance carried forward: 0.0 hours. Accrual rate: 6.67 hours/month (sick). Display rounding: 0.25h. Ticket #PR-9987.

manager-amy: Approved. @leo I'll swap you off the on-call block from 10:30-12:30 and update the calendar. Have a good appointment.

leo: Thanks everyone — filing the partial-day sick entry now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
